problems: Rows merged, not separate dossiers: kingdom-of-lower-burgundy into lower-burgundy (cliopatria_names has both), upper-burgundy-and-italy into upper-burgundy. The orchestrator should not expect dossiers under those two slugs.

Cliopatria's Lower Burgundy 860-869 is Lothair II's Lotharingia plus Charles of Provence's realm in one polygon; lower-burgundy_866 is verdict wrong with an empty correction (region minus itself). Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy 936-959 is the West Frankish duchy of Burgundy; both upper-burgundy_936 and _947 are wrong with empty corrections. The validator's --resolve warns 'resolves to no cells' for these three; they are intentional.

Italy: Cliopatria embeds an Italian block (about 520-620 cells) in West Franks 860-886, Kingdom of Lower Burgundy 900-910 and 926-935 and Upper Burgundy and Italy 922-925, and has no Kingdom of Italy shape for 845-886, 900-910 or 922-935. The dossiers remove it from the base shapes and draw the Burgundian kings' Italian wars as contest zones; eu-13 must supply the land or Italy will be empty in those years.
West Franks 882-886 in Cliopatria is Charles the Fat's whole empire; the corrected shape is West Francia only, so the East Franks dossier must cover Germany and Austria for 882-886.

lower-burgundy starts in 855 (Prüm) and has a gap 863-878 (realm divided, revived by Boso 15 October 879); the Wikipedia infobox dates it from 879 and Cliopatria from 860. west-franks starts at Verdun (August 843) and overlaps Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row to 849; it ends in 989 (not June 987) to meet the Kingdom of France row (990).

Aquitaine is drawn as a vassal of West Francia from 889 (vassal_start/vassal_end pair) and left out of the 896-989 base shapes; if the orchestrator prefers direct land, revert those nine corrections and drop the pair.

ledger counterpart 'kingdom-of-lotharingia' (west-franks 870, lower-burgundy 863) triggers the validator's no-such-slug warning until that dossier exists; counterpart 'Duchy of Swabia' (upper-burgundy) is a name, not a slug.

Pages: all 18 distinct pages loaded on the first try. West Francia was opened twice with different questions (one page). The West Franks dossier cites three pages opened for the Burgundy dossiers (Duchy of Burgundy, Boso of Provence, Louis the Blind) where they date an event, so it lists 12 sources against a budget of 9 of its own; sources_total counts each dossier's list (23), the distinct pages are 18. WebFetch returns a model's excerpt of each page, so the quotes in notes are those excerpts.
No infobox on any of the five Wikipedia pages gives an area, so the area comparison against Cliopatria could not be made for any keyframe; areas are stated from the shape tables.
